candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record confirms Candida tropicalis on CSF NGS with meningeal enhancement and brain parenchymal involvement (FLAIR hyperintensity, neuropsychiatric symptoms), establishing meningoencephalitis caused by Candida tropicalis. 'Meningitis, right-sided' captures only the meningeal inflammation component and omits the encephalitis component and the specific fungal etiology, making it an incomplete parent-level descriptor.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Meningitis is a component/parent category but lacks the specific etiology (Candida tropicalis) and the encephalitis component required by the benchmark

case_quality_flags: Concurrent anti-NMDAR and anti-AMPAR1 antibodies noted; autoimmune encephalitis co-diagnosis possible but CSF NGS Candida tropicalis supports primary infectious etiology as benchmark
Underlying otogenic source (otitis media/mastoiditis with bone destruction) provides plausible route of CNS invasion
